dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: *sigh* I've circled the village over and over again... I still can't remember anything...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Though the people and everything else here feel familiar... something seems to have gone missing ever since I've lost my Vision...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened to your Vision?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I turned it in a long time ago... The people from the Tenryou Commission marched up to the village to inspect and confiscate when the Vision Hunt Decree was first announced. I heard that the people who refused to cooperate had a really bad time.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: *sigh* I thought that I should just stay out of trouble. It wouldn't have been good to trouble the villagers...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: It's just that... though I only turned the Vision in, I feel like something has gone missing from inside me, too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Something from inside you?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Like... a kind of enthusiasm or obsession that I had. Maybe that was what has kept me in the village this entire time. But I can't remember any of it anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Why did I come here? Why did I stay? What should I be doing right now? What should I do next?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Amnesia? No, I couldn't call it that. I know who I am and who everyone is here. I remember every road and everything I've done in the village. I haven't forgotten anything.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's just that... All of this feels like they've lost their meaning after I lost the Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Never mind, go tend to your own business. I'm just rambling. I'll look around some more and give this some more thought...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Do you mean... before? Or now?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I helped out the villagers here and drove away Treasure Hoarders who were causing disturbances. Just little things that were within my power — nothing worth mentioning.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: But I can still vaguely remember that I was waiting here in this village for something important...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: It's just that I've almost completely forgotten what that was, so I have no idea why I stayed here...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: *sigh* Oh well... There's no reason to stay if I can't remember the reason for it. I might as well leave and go look around.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: How about you? You look to be an outlander. What brings you to Inazuma with the Sakoku Decree still in effect?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here to look for someone.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Inazuma has become quite a dangerous place. The person that you're searching for must be very important to you for you to be here right now...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: You want to speak with the Almighty Shogun? Uh... that really isn't something ordinary villagers like us can help you with. I suggest you ask around in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Yea, I should be leaving as well... Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you. How have your travels been?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Same old, same old. Though I've been waiting for her for most of my life, I still can't remember her voice or her looks. Something's awfully wrong with my head...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't beat yourself up over this...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: You know, that's the funny part. I can't even remember how she looks even though I loved her so much. And you'd think I would be sad.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: But for me, forgetting someone is the same as having all thoughts of them severed. I can't feel anything for them I can't even think of them.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: She's probably the one that's really sad, seeing as how I've completely forgotten about her...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Still, thanks for retrieving those journals. Even though I still have no recollection of her, it's good to know that I was once so determined.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I will continue to wait here for her. The me from before wouldn't have wanted to let her down...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, any more thoughts about the Vision Hunt Decree?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: When Lord Kujou came to collect our Visions, he said that this was a necessary step to achieve Eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I don't really understand these grand ideals... I'm just an ordinary person. But I guess Eternity is something that never changes?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Something that never changes... I feel like I'm very close to becoming something like that...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: My heart is like stagnant water due to the lack of drive and ambition. I can't feel sadness or happiness. It's like I'm dead inside...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I'm not sure if this is a good or bad thing. All I can do now is to accept it as my way of life.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Maybe something will change again if more extraordinary events occur... You know, such as your appearing in our village.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I wish you good luck. See you again.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: And good luck to you as well. We'll meet again!

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I remember now. Now that I have my Vision back, I remember everything.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I agreed to meet her in Konda Village, and we gave each other an omamori as a sign of that agreement. That's why I've been here all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I still remember that when we parted, I promised that I would wait for her forever, and that's how I came to be here. She must have done the same...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you received any news of her?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Uh, not yet...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: But I also wrote my experiences during the time when I had lost my Vision into my diary, just as I had before. When I meet her again, I'll share all of it with her.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I'll tell her about you too — about how you managed to reclaim my Vision... or should I say, reclaim "myself."

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Haha... To be honest, I've only just begun to realize as well that the important thing is not the "wish" itself, but the "right to wish."

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I thought that all I lost was everything concerning her, but in truth, I had also lost myself — the Tejima who waited, the Tejima who pursued.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: If not for your help, I might well have spent the rest of my life wandering aimlessly about...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you plan to do from here on out?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: That's a good question, and it's time I made some detailed plans. If I cannot keep waiting for her, then perhaps I shall leave the village in search of her after all.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Before, I wanted to leave because I felt lost. But this time, I'm making a move because I'm sure of what my goals must be.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Well, I've spent most of my life waiting to no avail, so I might as well be pro-active from here on out! It's not too late for an old man like me to learn from the determination of the young, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: As long as I hold my wish dearly in my heart, I will not lose my way. That's what you've taught me, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All the best to you. See you.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: See you, youngster. I hope that we will both find the person we are seeking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I hope all goes well with you.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I hope so too.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: As for you? Are you going to continue traveling?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: If so, please take these. These are some experiences from when I was younger that I've written down. Nothing would make me happier than if they could be of use to you.
